declaration.preface:
Solex Energy Limited is committed to respecting, protecting, and promoting labour and human rights across its operations and business relationships. The Company strives to provide a safe, healthy, inclusive, and respectful workplace that promotes fair working conditions, equal opportunity, employee development, open communication, and employee engagement.

Solex Energy Limited does not tolerate child labour, forced labour, human trafficking, discrimination, harassment, violence, abuse, exploitation, or any other violation of human rights. The Company is committed to complying with applicable labour and human rights laws and expects all employees, contractors, suppliers, and business partners to uphold these principles. Through responsible employment practices, training, grievance mechanisms, and continual improvement, the Company aims to protect employee dignity and foster a fair, safe, and productive workplace for all.
declaration.declaration: Solex Energy Limited has established key goals and commitments to strengthen workplace practices, enhance employee well-being, promote fair and inclusive employment, protect fundamental rights, and support continuous improvement across its operations.
declaration.scope:
This Policy applies to all employees, contractual workers, trainees, contractors, and other persons working on behalf of Solex Energy Limited. Where relevant, it also extends to suppliers, service providers, and business partners.

The Policy covers labour and human rights matters across the Company's operations, including occupational health and safety, fair working conditions, employee engagement and social dialogue, career development and training, prevention of child and forced labour, human trafficking, discrimination, harassment, and other forms of exploitation or abuse.

focusAreas: Respect for Human Rights & Human Dignity
Fair Employment, Workplace Practices & Employee Voice
Responsible Recruitment & Protection of Vulnerable Workers
Prevention of Child Labour, Forced Labour & Human Trafficking

Respect for Human Rights & Human Dignity: Solex Energy Limited prioritizes respect for fundamental human rights and the dignity of every individual associated with its operations. The Company aims to maintain a workplace free from abuse, intimidation, degrading treatment, and practices that may adversely affect individual rights. Human rights considerations are integrated into relevant employment and workplace practices, with expectations extended to contractors and business partners where appropriate.

Respect internationally recognized human rights in accordance with the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, UN Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights, and Constitution of India (Articles 14–23).
Prohibit forced, bonded, child labour, human trafficking, modern slavery, harassment, abuse, and discrimination.
Identify and address material human-rights risks across operations and relevant business relationships.
Respect freedom of association and collective bargaining in accordance with the Trade Unions Act, 1926 and Industrial Disputes Act, 1947.
Maintain confidential, accessible, and retaliation-free mechanisms for reporting human-rights concerns.
Safe & Healthy Workplace: Solex Energy Limited prioritizes the protection of employee health, safety, and wellbeing through systematic identification and management of workplace hazards. Key areas include safe operation of machinery and equipment, electrical safety, chemical handling, material movement, fire and emergency preparedness, personal protective equipment, workplace inspections, incident reporting, and safety awareness. The Company seeks to strengthen preventive measures and reduce workplace incidents through training and continual improvement.
Provide and maintain a safe and healthy workplace that prevents work-related injuries and occupational illnesses.
Identify and control risks related to manufacturing, electrical systems, machinery, chemicals, material handling, maintenance, warehousing, and logistics.
Apply the hierarchy of controls and provide appropriate PPE, training, and supervision.
Maintain effective controls for emergency preparedness, fire, electrical, machinery, chemical, and other material safety risks.
Monitor occupational health and provide appropriate medical checks for employees exposed to hazardous processes.
Fair Employment, Workplace Practices & E: Solex Energy Limited prioritizes fair and responsible employment practices covering wages, working hours, leave, benefits, workplace facilities, and other employment conditions. The Company encourages open communication between employees and management and provides appropriate opportunities for employees to provide feedback and raise workplace concerns. Respect for applicable freedom of association and collective representation rights is also promoted.
Provide clear employment terms and comply with applicable requirements relating to wages, working hours, overtime, leave, and statutory benefits.
Ensure timely payment of wages, appropriate payslips, and lawful wage deductions.
Prohibit unlawful withholding of wages and other unfair employment practices.
Respect freedom of association and collective bargaining where legally applicable.
Provide employees with appropriate channels for communication, participation, feedback, and raising concerns without retaliation.
Discipline, Dismissal & Termination: Solex Energy Limited prioritizes fair, consistent, and transparent approaches to disciplinary action, dismissal, resignation, and termination. Disciplinary measures are intended to be proportionate to the nature of the issue and implemented without physical punishment, threats, humiliation, or other degrading treatment. Employment separation is managed in accordance with applicable legal and contractual requirements, including appropriate communication and settlement processes.
Prohibit arbitrary dismissal, corporal punishment, coercion, intimidation, and degrading treatment.
Provide employees a fair opportunity to respond before disciplinary action is taken.
Apply the principles of natural justice in disciplinary matters.
Maintain appropriate documentation and consistent disciplinary procedures.
Ensure disciplinary action and termination comply with the Industrial Employment (Standing Orders) Act, 1946 and applicable legal requirements.
Learning, Professional Growth & Employee: Solex Energy Limited prioritizes continuous learning, technical and functional skill development, career progression, and employee wellbeing. Training needs are identified based on job responsibilities, performance, operational requirements, and emerging business needs. The Company aims to provide employees with opportunities to enhance their capabilities through induction, technical training, health and safety training, professional development, and performance feedback.
Provide appropriate induction, technical, functional, behavioural, and compliance-related training.
Support employee learning, skill development, professional growth, and career progression.
Conduct appropriate performance and development discussions for eligible employees.
Promote physical, psychological, and social wellbeing and address excessive stress, fatigue, and burnout.
Promote employee engagement, work-life balance, and responsible workload management.
Equality, Inclusion & Respectful Conduct: Solex Energy Limited prioritizes equal opportunity, diversity, inclusion, and respectful workplace behaviour. Employment decisions relating to recruitment, development, promotion, compensation, and career opportunities are intended to be based on relevant qualifications, skills, experience, performance, and business requirements. Discrimination, harassment, bullying, intimidation, and sexual harassment are not tolerated, and employees are encouraged to report concerns through established channels.
Provide equal opportunity in recruitment, employment, compensation, training, development, and career progression.
Prohibit discrimination, harassment, bullying, intimidation, and abuse based on protected characteristics.
Maintain zero tolerance for sexual harassment in accordance with the POSH Act, 2013, through the Site's Internal Complaints Committee (ICC).
Promote diversity, inclusion, and equal opportunities for women and underrepresented groups.
Maintain appropriate mechanisms for reporting and addressing discrimination and harassment concerns.
Responsible Recruitment & Protection of: Solex Energy Limited prioritizes responsible and transparent recruitment practices. Employment conditions should be clearly communicated to workers, and appropriate documentation and age-verification processes are maintained. Particular attention is given to protecting contract, temporary, migrant, young, and other vulnerable workers from unfair treatment, exploitation, unsafe conditions, or practices that may restrict their rights.
Maintain fair, transparent, and legally compliant recruitment and onboarding practices.
Verify the age, identity, and employment eligibility of employees and workers.
Prohibit child labour, forced labour, bonded labour, human trafficking, unlawful document retention, and unlawful recruitment fees.
Provide additional safeguards for vulnerable workers against exploitation, discrimination, and abuse.
Require relevant contractors, recruitment agencies, and labour-service providers to comply with applicable human-rights and labour requirements.
Grievance & Speak-Up Mechanisms: Solex Energy Limited prioritizes accessible and effective mechanisms through which employees and workers can raise grievances, workplace concerns, ethical issues, and human rights-related matters. Grievances are expected to be handled fairly, confidentially, and within appropriate timelines. The Company promotes a non-retaliatory environment so that individuals can raise concerns in good faith without fear of adverse consequences.
Provide accessible channels for raising concerns relating to workplace conditions, human rights, discrimination, harassment, health and safety, and unethical conduct.
Allow concerns to be raised through supervisors, Department Heads, Human Resources, EHS/Safety representatives, and established grievance or whistleblower mechanisms.
Maintain confidentiality and appropriately record, investigate, and address reported concerns.
Prohibit retaliation, intimidation, or adverse treatment against individuals raising concerns in good faith.
Escalate serious or systemic concerns to appropriate management or governance levels.
Prevention of Child Labour, Forced Labou: Solex Energy Limited prioritizes the prevention of child labour, forced or compulsory labour, bonded labour, human trafficking, slavery, and other forms of labour exploitation. The Company maintains appropriate recruitment and age-verification controls and expects workers to enter employment voluntarily. Relevant contractors, labour agencies, suppliers, and business partners are also expected to uphold these principles within their respective operations and employment practices.
Prohibit human trafficking and all forms of exploitation, including recruitment, transportation, or employment through force, coercion, deception, or abuse of vulnerability.
Prohibit child labour and ensure compliance with applicable minimum-age requirements.
Verify and document the age and identity of employees and workers during recruitment.
Prohibit forced, bonded, or involuntary labour, debt bondage, coercion, unlawful recruitment fees, and inappropriate document withholding.
Extend child labour, forced labour, and human trafficking requirements to relevant contractors, suppliers, subcontractors, and manpower agencies.
Investigate suspected violations and take appropriate corrective action, including safe removal and rehabilitation support where child labour is identified.

policy.monitoring:
Training effectiveness shall be periodically evaluated using assessments, feedback, observations, incident trends and other appropriate methods.

Transparent and regular reporting is essential for monitoring the effectiveness of this Policy, ensuring accountability, and supporting continual improvement. Solex Energy Limited shall implement the following reporting practices:

People, Labour & Human Rights Performance Reporting: Solex Energy Limited shall periodically review and report its performance against the commitments, objectives, targets, and key performance indicators established under this Policy. Reporting may include matters relating to human rights, health and safety, employee wellbeing, training, diversity and inclusion, grievances, recruitment practices, child labour and forced labour prevention, and compliance with applicable requirements.

Internal Reviews and Assessments: Solex Energy Limited shall conduct periodic reviews, assessments, and audits, as applicable, to evaluate compliance with this Policy and related procedures. Findings shall be documented and appropriate corrective and preventive actions shall be implemented where necessary.

Incident, Grievance and Concern Reporting: Solex Energy Limited shall maintain appropriate records of reported grievances, human rights concerns, workplace incidents, employee complaints, discrimination or harassment concerns, and other relevant matters. Significant or material issues shall be escalated to the appropriate level of management for review and action.

Management Reporting: Performance results, significant incidents, grievance trends, corrective actions, compliance issues, and emerging risks shall be periodically reported to Senior Management and relevant governance bodies, as applicable. Management shall review such information to assess the effectiveness of controls and identify opportunities for improvement.

Stakeholder Feedback: Solex Energy Limited shall consider relevant feedback received from employees, workers, contractors, suppliers, customers, communities, and other stakeholders. Where appropriate, such feedback shall be used to strengthen workplace practices, human rights management, employee wellbeing initiatives, and Policy implementation.

Public Disclosure: Solex Energy Limited may disclose relevant information regarding its people, labour and human rights performance through sustainability reports, ESG disclosures, annual reports, the Company website, or other approved communication channels, in accordance with applicable disclosure requirements and while protecting confidential and personal information.

Any employee, contractor, worker, supplier or other relevant stakeholder who becomes aware of a potential violation of this Policy may raise a concern through available Company reporting mechanisms, including direct reporting to the immediate supervisor or Department Head, reporting to the Human Resources Manager, reporting to the designated EHS / Safety representative for health and safety matters, use of the Company's established grievance or whistleblower mechanisms, or escalation to senior management or the appropriate governance body for serious, unresolved or systemic concerns.

Solex strictly prohibits retaliation, intimidation, discrimination or adverse treatment against any person who raises a concern or reports a suspected violation in good faith.

Reported concerns shall be handled appropriately and confidentially, subject to applicable legal and procedural requirements.
policy.reviewMechanism:
Human Resources Manager shall review this People, Labour & Human Rights Policy annually to ensure its continued relevance, effectiveness, and alignment with applicable legal, regulatory, operational, and stakeholder requirements.

The review shall consider performance against established targets, grievance trends, human rights and labour-related concerns, employee feedback, audit findings, workplace incidents, compliance obligations, and other relevant information.

The Policy shall be updated, where necessary, to reflect changes in applicable laws, regulations, Company procedures, business operations, workforce requirements, or identified risks and improvement opportunities. Significant updates shall be communicated to relevant employees and stakeholders.
